advisor.hack_morning_katabatic_window: Schedule exposed ridge hikes & Zodiac landings in the morning window — local katabatic downdrafts intensify sharply after solar noon.
advisor.hack_calving_surge_standoff: Maintain a > 15 m vertical/horizontal buffer from shoreline tide lines near active glacier fronts to avoid sudden calving tsunami surges.
advisor.hack_wet_landing_layering: Pull waterproof shell trousers OVER (never tucked inside) knee-high rubber boots so knee-deep Zodiac surf splashes drain outward.
advisor.hack_penguin_highway_5m: Keep >= 5 m from wildlife and never step into packed snow trenches ('penguin highways') — penguins have absolute right-of-way.
advisor.hack_biosecurity_boot_scrub: Vacuum Velcro cuffs, pockets, and tripod legs before first landing and scrub boot treads in Virkon biocide between every site.
advisor.hack_lithium_chest_pocket: Sub-zero wind chill drains camera & phone batteries by 60%+ — store spare batteries against body heat and seal optics in dry bags before re-entering warm cabins to prevent lens condensation.
advisor.hack_drake_midship_cabin: During Tier 3–5 Drake swells, secure loose cabin gear, stay on lower midship decks near the ship’s center of pitch/roll, and keep one hand free on railings.
advisor.hack_high_plateau_acclimatize: Polar atmospheric thinning above 2,000 m lowers barometric oxygen ~12% further than mid-latitude peaks — pace ascents conservatively and hydrate with insulated flasks.
advisor.hack_november_pack_ice_buffer: Early austral spring (Oct–Nov) fast ice frequently blocks narrow channels like Lemaire or Weddell approaches — keep 1–2 flexible buffer days in your schedule.
advisor.hack_polar_day_sleep_mask: 24-hour Midnight Sun disrupts circadian recovery before strenuous hikes — pack a contoured blackout sleep mask while enjoying golden-hour light around 23:00–02:00.

legal.disclaimerBody: Weather forecasts, sea-ice baselines, Bedmap3 subglacial interpolations, and T1–T5 hiking difficulty ratings are macro-scale scientific estimates for educational planning only. They CANNOT detect local hidden crevasses, avalanche slabs, or sudden micro-scale blizzards, and never substitute certified Expedition Leader or Ship Master authority.
legal.legalPageTitle: Terms of Service, GDPR Privacy Notice & Polar Safety Disclaimer
legal.liabilitySectionTitle: 1. Polar Expedition & Hiking Advisory Liability Limitation
legal.liabilitySectionBody: Antarctica Atlas provides open-science geospatial visualizations and automated route assessments on an 'AS IS' educational basis. Field conditions south of 60°S change rapidly and pose lethal hypothermia, crevasse, and marine hazards. Users assume full personal responsibility and must follow licensed IAATO Expedition Leaders, vessel captains, and national Antarctic program directives at all times.
legal.privacySectionBody: We do not use third-party advertising trackers. Access logs hash visitor identifiers with a daily rotating cryptographic salt and mask IP subnets (/24 IPv4, /48 IPv6) solely for aggregate service improvement. Registered users may export GPX plans or permanently erase their account and all stored itineraries at any time from the Account drawer.
legal.termsSectionTitle: 3. Open Data Attribution & Non-Commercial API Notice
legal.termsSectionBody: Users retain full ownership of uploaded GPX/GeoJSON/CSV itineraries. Underlying scientific datasets are credited under CC BY 4.0 (BAS Bedmap3, SCAR GeoMAP/ADD/CGA, COMNAP, NSIDC, Open-Meteo).
